title: A live-imaging protocol for tracking receptor dynamics in single cells
protocol: Defrost cells in 37°C water bath for 3 minutes.
Equally split defrosted cell liquid into two 10 cm dishes containing 10 mL of culture medium and incubate in a 5% CO2 incubator at 37°C for 12 hours.
Pre-coat each 35 mm glass coverslip bottom dish with 200 μL of 10 mg/mL Poly-L-Lysine diluted 1:1000 in ultrapure distilled water.
Incubate the pre-coated dishes at 37°C for one hour.
Wash each 35 mm glass base dish three times with 200 μL of 37°C PBS.
Remove cells from two 10 cm dishes by washing each dish once with 2 mL of 37°C HBSS.
Add 2 mL of 37°C Trypsin to detach the cells in a 5% CO2 incubator at 37°C for 2 minutes.
Neutralize Trypsin with 2 mL of 37°C TNS, then transfer the cell mixture from each dish to one 50 mL tube.
Centrifuge the tubes at 210 × g for 5 minutes at 25°C.
Aspirate the supernatant and add 10 mL of 37°C Cell culture medium (medium+10%FBS) to suspend cells.
Count the cell number, transfer 5 × 10^4 cells to each 1.5 mL tube, and centrifuge at 210 × g for 5 minutes at 25°C.
Transfer 400 μL culture medium into pre-prepared 1.5 mL tube.
Transfer 3 mL buffer E into Neon tube.
Insert the Neon tube into Neon Pipette Station.
Aspirate the cell-DNA mixture into 10 μL Neon tip.
Place the Neon pipette into Neon Pipette Station.
Turn on the Neon device and enter electroporation parameters: Pulse voltage 1,560 V, Pulse 5 ms, Pulse number 10, Cell density 5 × 10^6 cells/mL Transfection efficiency 90%, tip type 10 μL.
Fill the Neon tube with 3 mL buffer E.
Insert the Neon tube into the Neon Pipette Station until it “clicks” into place.
Add 1.5 μg/35 mm glass coverslip bottom dish AT1-EGFP and 0.5 μg/35 mm glass coverslip bottom dish mScarlet-LOX-1 to a 1.5 mL tube containing cells, then mix gently.
Insert a 10 μL Neon tip into the Neon pipette.
Press the push-button on the Neon pipette to the first stop and immerse the Neon tip into the cell-DNA mixture.
Slowly release the push-button on the pipette to aspirate the cell-DNA mixture into the Neon tip.
Insert the Neon pipette with the sample vertically into the Neon tube in the Neon Pipette Station until it “clicks” into place.
Press Start button on the Neon device touchscreen.
Remove the Neon pipette from the Neon Pipette Station when electroporation is complete.
Immediately transfer the sample mixture from the Neon tip into a prepared 1.5 mL tube containing 400 μL Cell culture medium (medium+10%FBS).
Transfer 200 μL cell suspension from the 1.5 mL tube into each pre-coated 35 mm glass coverslip bottom dish.
Incubate the dishes in a 5% CO2 incubator at 37°C for 12 hours.
Check optimal electroporation parameters based on cell types.
Use each Neon tip only once to ensure reproducibility and eliminate variation of transfection conditions within or between experiments.
Discard used Neon tips into an appropriate biological hazardous waste container.
Wash the sample dish three times with pre-warmed 37°C imaging buffer.
Keep the sample dish ready for microscopic observation before initiating the process.
Turn on the super-resolution microscope and connect it securely to the PC software cellSens Dimension 1.11 (Olympus, Japan).
Activate the 488 nm (green) and 561 nm (red) laser channels at 20% power.
Adjust the laser power according to image brightness.
Set the film recording time to a total of 5 minutes, with 60 cycles and a 5-second interval between each cycle.
Enable the auto focus feature.
Add a drop of lens oil to the 100× NA 1.49 objective.
Place the sample dish on the microscope stage and fix it with the matching clamp.
Turn on the heater provided by the manufacturer (STX Series Stage Top Incubator System, Tokai Hit, Japan) to maintain the temperature at 37°C.
Under the EYE1DIC mode, adjust the focus to obtain clear images of the cells.
Switch to the EYE2-G (green channel) or EYE3-R (red channel) to check fluorescence expression and locate a single target cell.
Select the cell area.
Click “Start” to initiate image recording.
Add 100 μL of stimulus (1/10 final concentration diluted by imaging buffer) or vehicle to the sample dish just after a 1-min image has been captured.
Use imaging buffer and oxLDL as vehicle and stimulus respectively in this protocol.
Preincubate cells for 1 min before stimulation.
Stimulate cells with 10 μg/mL oxLDL.
Capture images of cells before (0 min) and 3 min after stimulation.
Subtract green and red channel backgrounds using the 3D deconvolution algorithm of cellSens Dimension 1.11.
Combine processed channels to form merged image.
Maintain consistent laser settings and microscope configuration between conditions for high-quality quantitative data.
Find an optimal visualization of the cell in both the green and red channels.
Ensure clear green and red puncta are visible and moving temporally.
If necessary, switch to microscope eyepiece mode to locate cells manually.
Place the microscope shade plate in push-in position before switching modes.
Add the stimulus gently to the sample dish without disturbing the selected area.
Cease the imaging cycle if focus alteration is required for drug addition.
Stimulate slowly by pushing the pipette to release reagent to the periphery of the dish.
Use a perfusion device as an alternative method for adding stimuli.
Perform bleach correction on captured images prior to analysis if needed.
